attribution_limitations: The text prints an LVEF of 51% for the clinic echocardiogram while Tables 1 and 2 print 0.52 for the 6 March 2022 echocardiogram. The source makes these the same examination (the text cites Table 2 for it; its IVS, LVPW, LA, LV, E/e’ and pulmonary artery systolic pressure equal the 6 March 2022 row; Figure 2A dates the same IVS and LVPW to 6 March 2022), so the two numbers are a source conflict: both values are review_only and neither is chosen.

Table 2 prints global longitudinal strain on 22 March 2022 and April 2022 without a minus sign (10.0%, 13.4%) while the text and Table 1 print GLS − 10% and GLS − 13.4% for the same examinations; a one-character sign difference treated as an ambiguity. The observations carry the negative values printed in the text and Table 1; the Table 2 cells are not corrected and stay as printed in the measurement series.
The text labels the left ventricular posterior wall abbreviation as LVPM in one sentence while tables use LVPW; the same value 9.88 mm is read as the posterior wall thickness.

Table 1 reports the ECT 99m Tc-PYP result as CA of ATTR subtypes while the text reports bisphosphonate scintigraphy with Perugini grade 2 and the final diagnosis as light chain (lambda) cardiac amyloidosis; the source does not state that the two scintigraphy descriptions are the same study, so they are kept as separate observations and no ATTR diagnosis is recorded.
The final regimen lists furosemide/torasemide as one entry; whether one or both loop diuretics were given is not stated.

The text does not date the clinic visit or the extracardiac biopsy; dates and hospitalization membership come from Table 1 (rowspan hospitalization cells). The cMRI text says 1 month later while Table 1 places it in the April 2022 hospitalization; no further timing is inferred.

Figure 2C caption dates the thickened echocardiogram 21 May 2022 while Table 2 gives May 2022 for the matching IVS 12.3 mm and LVPW 12.6 mm values; both are consistent and recorded as one measurement.
The discussion suggests the normal wall thickness could be due to the patient’s short stature (150 cm); this is a hedged author explanation, not a recorded cause.

Qualitative findings of the clinic echocardiogram that only the text states (restrictive transmitral flow, grade 3 diastolic dysfunction, non-dilated left ventricle, no granular sparkling echotexture, mild pericardial effusion) carry no time: the text does not date them and no Table 1 or Table 2 cell states them. Only values that a dated table cell also states take the 6 March 2022 time.

The discussion sentence on biomarkers ("elevated NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity troponin levels") is undated and its scope over troponin is not clear; in the case text "elevated" qualifies only the NT-proBNP level, so the troponin I observation keeps flag unknown.
